mainTopic: A נכרי's semen, a מצורעת's דם טהרה, and the first discharge of a minor זב and of a מצורע
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a Jew's שכבת זרע is טמא wherever it is, but a נכרי's is טהור wherever it is, except for urine mixed in with it. Since that urine is only טמא מדרבנן, the גמרא proves that a נכרי's semen is pure even מדרבנן. The ברייתא cannot settle רב פפא's question about a Jew's semen inside a גויה, because he was asking about the time after three days, and that question ends in תיקו. Next the גמרא explains the dispute in the משנה about a מצורעת's דם טהרה. בית הלל learn from ״לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה״, using a קל וחומר and אם אינו ענין, that her דם טהרה is impure. בית שמאי break the קל וחומר, or say ״לַזָּכָר״ is needed to include a minor זב. The גמרא then proves that a minor זב's first discharge makes things impure by touch, just like an adult's. Finally, רב יוסף asks whether a מצורע's first discharge makes things impure by carrying, and רבא begins a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a Jew's semen is impure everywhere, a נכרי's is pure everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא as proof. A Jew's semen is טמא even inside a גויה. A נכרי's semen is טהור even inside a Jewish woman, except for the urine mixed with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: …even inside a non-Jewish woman. But a non-Jew's semen is pure wherever it is, even inside a Jewish woman, except for the urine that is in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that it brings as proof about a נכרי's semen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up two opposite rules. A Jew's שכבת זרע stays טמא no matter whose body it is in. A נכרי's semen stays טהור no matter whose body it is in. The one exception is urine mixed in with the נכרי's semen, which is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Semen, which can make things impure
Inside the body (womb) of a non-Jewish woman
A non-Jew
Urine

steps.confusionAlert: The step begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'even inside a non-Jewish woman' finish the ברייתא's first rule, which is about a Jew's semen. That rule is quoted in full in step 5.

phrases.english: even inside a non-Jewish woman.
And that of a non-Jew is pure in every place,
even inside a Jewish woman,
except for the urine that is in it.
phrases.notes: He means urine that got mixed in with the non-Jew's semen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא quoted just before this section as proof about a נכרי's semen.
steps.raayaObject: That a נכרי's semen is pure even inside a Jewish woman
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting a Jew's semen with a נכרי's

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא only means pure by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible way to escape the proof: maybe the ברייתא only means the semen is pure מדאורייתא, while it is still טמא מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: here too, it means pure by Torah law, but impure by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is anticipating a pushback against its own proof. It is setting up a reply that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that 'pure' in the ברייתא only describes the Torah level. If so, the ברייתא proves nothing about whether חז"ל made the semen impure.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: And if you will say: here too,
it is pure by Torah law,
but impure by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הָכִי נָמֵי טְהוֹרָה מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible weakness in the proof from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the semen is pure even מדרבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Pure' might only mean pure on the Torah level

steps.title: The urine is only rabbinically impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on that idea. The ברייתא calls the urine טמא, yet that urine is not טמא מדאורייתא. So the ברייתא must be speaking on the rabbinic level.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say her urine is impure by Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the pushback from step 2 with a sharp question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts the pure semen with the impure urine. That urine is only טמא because of a rabbinic rule. So the contrast only makes sense if the ברייתא is talking on the rabbinic level. That means 'pure' has to mean pure even מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question expecting 'no')
Make things impure

phrases.english: Is that to say her urine,
phrases.notes: This is the non-Jew's urine that got mixed in and is now inside the Jewish woman.

phrases.english: makes things impure by Torah law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ מֵי רַגְלֶיהָ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מִי מְטַמְּאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pushback raised in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא means pure only מדאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'except for urine' clause names something that is only rabbinically impure, so the whole ברייתא must be speaking on the rabbinic level.

steps.title: Conclusion: a נכרי's semen is pure even rabbinically
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a נכרי's semen is pure even מדרבנן, and it accepts this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: it is pure even by rabbinic law. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its final conclusion from the ברייתא and agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the 'Torah level only' escape is closed, the proof stands. A נכרי's semen inside a Jewish woman does not make anything impure, not even מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: A נכרי's semen is pure even מדרבנן. Only urine mixed in with it is טמא, and that urine is only טמא on a rabbinic level.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
it is pure even by rabbinic law.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינָּה: טְהוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion now that the objection has been answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נכרי's semen is טהור even מדרבנן.

steps.title: Trying to answer רב פפא's question from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the first half of the ברייתא. It suggests that this half settles רב פפא's question about a Jew's semen inside a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: a Jew's semen is impure everywhere, even inside a non-Jewish woman. Let us settle what רב פפא asked, for רב פפא asked: what is the law of a Jew's semen inside a non-Jewish woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new line. It tries to use the same ברייתא to answer a question that רב פפא asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא was unsure whether a Jew's semen stays טמא once it is inside a non-Jewish woman. The ברייתא seems to say outright that it is טמא even there, so the question would appear to be answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us resolve (a question)
Asked (raised a question he could not decide)
What is the law?

phrases.english: The master said:
The semen of a Jew
is impure in every place,
even inside a non-Jewish woman.
Let us resolve what רב פפא asked,
for רב פפא asked:
The semen of a Jew
inside a non-Jewish woman, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first half of the ברייתא from step 1 for a new purpose.
steps.raayaObject: An answer to רב פפא's question
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first rule of the ברייתא: a Jew's semen is impure even inside a גויה

steps.title: רב פפא asked only about after three days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Within three days the semen is clearly טמא, and that is what the ברייתא means. רב פפא's question was about what happens after three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Within three days, רב פפא had no question. His question was: after three days, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the attempted proof by narrowing exactly what רב פפא was asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא can be read as talking about the first three days after relations, when the semen is clearly טמא. רב פפא was asking about the time after three days. The ברייתא does not address that time, so his question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Within three days
He did not have a question about this
After three days

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say the ברייתא is wrong. It only says the ברייתא is talking about a different time period than רב פפא's question.

phrases.english: Within three days —
רב פפא had no question,
where he had a question —
after three days, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה — לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the ברייתא to settle רב פפא's question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may only mean within three days, while רב פפא asked about after three days.

steps.title: The two sides of the question about a non-Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two ways of looking at the question: does semen spoil within three days inside a גויה, as it does inside a Jewish woman?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: Jewish women, who are careful about מצוות, have hot bodies, so the semen spoils. Non-Jewish women, who are not careful about מצוות, do not have hot bodies, so it does not spoil. Or maybe: since they eat repugnant creatures and creeping animals, their bodies are also hot and it spoils?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two possible sides of a question about whether semen spoils inside a גויה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says a Jewish woman's worry about keeping מצוות heats her body, and that heat makes the semen spoil. A גויה lacks that worry, so the semen may stay fresh. Side two says her diet of שקצים and רמשים heats her body anyway, so the result would be the same.

keyTerms.meaning: they worry / are anxious about
their bodies are hot
becomes foul, spoils
repugnant creatures and creeping animals
or perhaps (introduces the other side)

phrases.english: Jewish women, who are anxious about מצוות —
their bodies are hot, and it becomes foul,
phrases.notes: "It" means the semen inside her. It spoils within three days.

phrases.english: non-Jews, who are not anxious about מצוות —
their bodies are not hot, and it does not become foul;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאָכְלִי שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים —
phrases.english: or perhaps: since they eat repugnant creatures and creeping animals —
their bodies are hot, and it becomes foul?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the question that follows the rejection in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does semen spoil within three days inside a גויה just as it does inside a Jewish woman?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question is left open with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two sides, so it closes the question with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides make sense and no source settles the matter. תיקו means the question stays open. It does not mean either side was proven.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand (the question remains unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: Whether semen spoils within three days inside a גויה is left unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question raised in step 7 without an answer.

steps.title: What is בית הלל's source for the blood of a מצורעת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the blood of a מצורעת during her days of טהרה and asks for the reason behind בית הלל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The blood of purity of a female leper: בית שמאי say, etc." What is the reason of בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks where בית הלל get the idea that this blood is impure, which sets up רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a woman gives birth, blood from her days of טהרה is normally pure. בית הלל nevertheless treat this blood as impure when the woman is a מצורעת. The גמרא wants to know what source they rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: blood seen during the days of purity after childbirth
a woman with צרעת (leper)
what is the reason / source?

phrases.english: The blood of purity of a female leper:
בית שמאי, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." points to the rest of the משנה. בית שמאי call the blood pure, and בית הלל call it impure.

phrases.english: What is the reason of בית הלל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The biblical source for בית הלל's ruling that a מצורעת's blood of טהרה is impure.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: the source is "male" and "female"
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from ״לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ that the bodily flows of a male and a female מצורע are included in the impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: "For the male" comes to include a male leper in his flows. "And for the female" comes to include a female leper in her flows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question by pointing to two words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word adds something. "Male" includes the flows of a מצורע, and "female" includes the flows of a מצורעת. Exactly what the extra word about the female includes is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: to include (an extra case learned from the פסוק)
his sources / bodily flows
a man with צרעת

phrases.english: רבי יצחק said:
"For the male" — to include a male leper regarding his flows,
"And for the female" — to include a female leper regarding her flows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words ״לַזָּכָר״ and ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ include the flows of a מצורע and a מצורעת.

steps.title: Which "flows" of the female are meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what "her flows" refers to. It cannot mean her other flows, because those are already learned from the male.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are "her flows"? If you say her other flows, that is already learned from the male!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses on רבי יצחק's reading to show that ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ must be teaching something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her saliva and urine work just like a man's. Since the male case already teaches those, ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ would be extra if it only covered them. So it must be teaching something that only a woman has.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (a first suggestion, about to be rejected)
the rest, the other
it is derived / it comes out

phrases.english: What are "her flows"?
If you say her other flows —
phrases.notes: Such as her saliva and urine.

phrases.english: that is derived from the male!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of רבי יצחק's derivation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it means her saliva and urine, the word is not needed, since those are already learned from the male.

steps.title: "Her flows" means her blood of טהרה
steps.stepSummary: ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ comes to make her blood of טהרה impure. That is the source for בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for her blood, to make her blood of purity impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra word for the female covers her blood. This gives בית הלל their source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is something only the woman has, so it cannot be learned from the male. That makes ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ needed to teach that a מצורעת's blood of טהרה is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (introduces the correct answer)
to make impure

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל learn from ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ that a מצורעת's blood of טהרה is impure.

phrases.english: Rather, it is for her blood,
to make her blood of purity impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the extra word includes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Her flows" might mean her saliva and urine.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means her blood of טהרה, which only a woman has.

steps.title: And how do בית שמאי read the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בית שמאי, who call the blood pure, do with ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking how בית שמאי understand the extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ teaches that her blood is impure, then בית שמאי, who say it is pure, seem to go against the פסוק. They must read the word some other way.

phrases.english: And בית שמאי?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what do they do with the word ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from בית הלל's reading to the other side of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How בית שמאי explain ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ if they hold the blood is pure.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the female cannot be learned from the male
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that a female cannot be learned from a male מצורע, because the male has stricter rules. So ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ is needed just for her saliva and urine.
steps.simpleTranslation: A female cannot be learned from a male, because one can refute it: the male is special, since he must grow his hair, tear his clothes, and is forbidden in marital relations. Can you say the same about a female, who does not have these rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for בית שמאי. The male case cannot teach about the female, so the word ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ is used up teaching about her ordinary flows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male מצורע has extra strict rules: hair grown long, torn clothes, no marital relations. A מצורעת does not have these. So one cannot assume his flows' impurity carries over to her. That means ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ is needed for her saliva and urine, and nothing is left over to teach about her blood.

keyTerms.meaning: to refute (to point out a difference that breaks the comparison)
letting the hair grow long
tearing one's clothes
marital relations
what about... which is special because (a refutation formula)

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי agree that the word ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ teaches something. They just say it teaches about her saliva and urine, not her blood.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי say a female מצורעת cannot be learned from a male, so ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ is needed for her saliva and urine and does not teach about her blood. בית הלל answer in the next steps by turning the reasoning around: the male can be learned from the female.

phrases.english: A female cannot be derived from a male,
since there is room to refute:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְזָכָר שֶׁכֵּן טָעוּן פְּרִיעָה וּפְרִימָה,
phrases.english: What about a male? He is special, since he must let his hair grow and tear his clothes,
and he is forbidden in marital relations;
will you say the same of a female, who does not have these?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקֵבָה מִזָּכָר לָא אָתְיָא, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by rejecting the assumption from step 11 that the female can be learned from the male.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The male's stricter rules break the comparison, so ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ is needed for her saliva and urine, and not for her blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל comes down to one point: whether the male case can teach about the female.

steps.title: בית הלל: the male can be learned from the female
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer בית שמאי: the תורה did not need to write ״לַזָּכָר״, because a male מצורע can be learned from a female by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do בית הלל say? The תורה could have written only the female and not needed the male, because I would reason this way: a female doesn't grow her hair wild or tear her clothes, and she isn't forbidden in marital relations, and still the תורה made her flows impure. A male, who has all these stricter rules, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בית הלל respond to בית שמאי's reading from Step 14. בית הלל build a קל וחומר showing that the male's flows did not need their own word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male מצורע has stricter rules than a female: he grows his hair wild, tears his clothes, and may not be with his wife. So if even the lighter female's flows are impure, the stricter male's flows must be impure too. That means the word ״לַזָּכָר״ is extra, and Step 16 shows what it teaches instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter case: if the light case has a rule, the strict case surely does
Literally 'springs'; here the body's flows, such as saliva and urine
'Not all the more so?', the closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: The female is the lighter case here, so the reasoning runs from female to male. Don't flip it around.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?
Let the Merciful One write it about the female alone,
and there would be no need for the male,
and I would reason:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה נְקֵבָה, שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה פְּרִיעָה וּפְרִימָה,
phrases.english: If a female, who does not need to grow her hair wild or tear her clothes,
and is not forbidden in marital relations,
the Merciful One still included her flows as impure,
then a male, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל? לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּנְקֵבָה וְלָא בָּעֵי זָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's claim in Step 14 that the female cannot be learned from the male, by showing the male can be learned from the female.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's reading that ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״ is needed only for saliva and urine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the male can be learned by קל וחומר from the female, then ״לַזָּכָר״ is extra and must teach something new.

steps.title: The extra word teaches that her דם טהרה is impure
steps.stepSummary: Because ״לַזָּכָר״ is not needed for the male, it is moved to the female. Since her flows are already taught, it teaches that her דם טהרה is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the word ״לַזָּכָר״ is not needed for the male, use it for the female. And if it is not needed for her flows, use it for her blood, to make her דם טהרה impure.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל finish their argument. They show where the extra word goes and what it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule אם אינו ענין: a word that isn't needed in its own place is moved to a nearby topic. Here it moves twice. First from the male to the female. Then, since her flows are already covered, it moves to her blood, which makes her דם טהרה impure. This is how בית הלל reach their ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it is not needed for this topic': a rule that moves an extra word in a פסוק to a related topic
'Apply it to the topic of...'
Blood a woman sees during the days of purity after birth

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: the male is learned by קל וחומר from the female, so ״לַזָּכָר״ is moved over to teach that a מצורעת's דם טהרה is impure.

phrases.english: If the word “male” is not needed for the male,
apply it to the female;
and if it is not needed for her flows,
phrases.notes: Her other flows are already taught by ״וְלַנְּקֵבָה״, as רבי יצחק said in Step 10.

phrases.english: apply it to her blood,
to make her blood of purity impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן ״לְזָכָר״ — תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לִנְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the argument begun in Step 15 by showing what the now-extra word teaches.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For בית הלל, the extra ״לַזָּכָר״ teaches that a מצורעת's דם טהרה is impure.

steps.title: בית שמאי break the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say the male cannot be learned from the female, because the female is stricter in one way: she becomes impure even from flows caused by outside factors.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do בית שמאי say? A male cannot be learned from a female, because the reasoning can be broken: the female is special because she becomes impure even from אונס. Can you say the same about a male, who does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how בית שמאי answer בית הלל: they knock down the קל וחומר with a פירכא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'lighter' case is lighter in every way. A woman becomes a זבה even when the flow was caused by something outside her control, but a man does not become a זב that way. So the female is stricter in one area, the male is not simply 'stricter', and the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Something beyond one's control; here a flow caused by an outside factor
'Can you say...?', the closing words of a refutation

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai?
The male cannot be learned from the female,
since it can be refuted:
What about a female, who becomes impure even from an outside cause?
Can you say the same of a male, who does not?

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכָר מִנְּקֵבָה לָא אָתֵיא, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from female to male
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The female is stricter in one area (impurity from אונס), so she is not simply the lighter case.

steps.title: בית הלל: that refutation comes from the wrong topic
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל object that we are dealing with מצורע, so a refutation taken from the laws of זב doesn't count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do בית הלל say? We are dealing with a מצורע, and you refute with the laws of a זב?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל push back against בית שמאי's refutation from Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about אונס belongs to זב and זבה, a different kind of impurity. בית הלל argue that a קל וחומר about מצורע should only be broken by differences inside the laws of מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: A man made impure by a certain kind of bodily discharge
'We are standing', meaning we are dealing with this topic

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?
We are dealing with a leper,
and they refute with matters of a zav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the refutation of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's refutation based on impurity from אונס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The refutation comes from the laws of זב, a different topic than מצורע, so it shouldn't break a קל וחומר about מצורע.

steps.title: בית שמאי: both are kinds of impurity
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that both מצורע and זב come under the shared heading of impurity, so a difference from זב can still break the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what do בית שמאי say? They refute based on the shared name 'impurity'.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי defend their refutation against בית הלל's objection in Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי see מצורע and זב as part of one wider family: טומאה. So if the female is stricter in one kind of impurity, she is not simply 'lighter' in impurity, and the קל וחומר still fails. The disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל comes down to how wide a refutation may reach.

keyTerms.meaning: The shared heading 'impurity' that includes both מצורע and זב

steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to one question: can the laws of זב refute a קל וחומר about מצורע? בית שמאי say yes, since both are טומאה. בית הלל say no.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai?
They refute based on the shared name of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 18 and defends Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the category: מצורע and זב both fall under טומאה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A refutation from זב laws doesn't apply to a קל וחומר about מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since both are טומאה, a difference in one can refute a קל וחומר in the other.

steps.title: Another answer: בית שמאי need ״לַזָּכָר״ to include even a young boy
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי can also say that ״לַזָּכָר״ is not extra at all. It teaches that any male, adult or minor, falls under the laws of זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, בית שמאי can say to you: that word ״לַזָּכָר״ is needed for something else. ״לַזָּכָר״ means any male, whether an adult or a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer for בית שמאי. It says the word ״לַזָּכָר״ is already being used for another lesson, so בית הלל cannot take it to teach about דם טהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 15–16, בית הלל said ״לַזָּכָר״ was extra and moved it to teach that דם טהרה is impure. The first answer (Steps 17–19) attacked the קל וחומר. This answer takes a different path: the word is not extra, because it teaches that even a young boy can become a זב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say', which introduces a second, different answer
It is needed for something else, so it is not extra
Whether an adult or a minor

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not take back the earlier answer. It is a separate, second way to defend בית שמאי.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Beit Shammai can say to you:
That word "for a male" is needed for something else,
"for a male" means anyone who is a male,
whether an adult or a minor.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. It doesn't change the meaning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, אָמְרִי לָךְ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent defense of בית שמאי, alongside the answer in Steps 17–19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word in question is already being used for another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לַזָּכָר״ is extra, so it can be moved to teach that דם טהרה is impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לַזָּכָר״ teaches that males of any age can be a זב, so it is not free for another teaching.

steps.title: בית הלל learn about minors from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל learn that a minor can be a זב from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״, so for them ״לַזָּכָר״ is still free to teach about דם טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? They learn it from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״, which includes both adult and child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בית הלל deal with this, and answers that they learn the minor from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״ already teaches that a minor can be a זב, בית הלל don't need ״לַזָּכָר״ for that. So for them, ״לַזָּכָר״ is still extra and can teach about דם טהרה. The disagreement is really about which פסוק is the source for including a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn it from (another source)
'This is the law of the זב' (ויקרא 15:32)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: ״לַזָּכָר״ includes minors. בית הלל: minors come from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״, so ״לַזָּכָר״ is free to teach that דם טהרה is impure.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?
They derive it from "This is the law of the zav":
whether an adult or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how בית הלל still have ״לַזָּכָר״ free, even after בית שמאי's claim in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source for the same law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״לַזָּכָר״, we would have no source that a minor can be a זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל learn about minors from ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks: does a young זב's first discharge make things impure by touch?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks whether the first discharge of a minor זב makes things impure by touch, since the פסוק places זיבה next to semen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: when ריש לקיש taught the laws of זב, he asked this: what about the first discharge of a young זב? Does it make things impure by touch? After all, the תורה says ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב וַאֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע״.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a minor can be a זב, the גמרא opens a new question about one detail of a young זב. This step sets up the question, and the next step lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an adult, the first discharge makes things impure by touch, like semen does. The פסוק mentions the זב together with semen. So maybe the first discharge works like semen, which raises a problem for a boy whose semen doesn't make anything impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The first discharge (sighting) of זיבה
A זב who is a young boy
Touch, meaning impurity passed on by contact
Semen
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פָשֵׁיט רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ בְּזָב,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish was teaching the laws of a zav,
he asked this question:
the first discharge of a zav who is a minor,
does it make things impure through touch?

phrases.aramaic: ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב וַאֲשֶׁר תֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת זָרַע״
phrases.english: "This is the law of the zav, and of him from whom semen goes out"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:32. The פסוק puts the זב right next to semen, and that's the point of the question.

phrases.english: is what the Torah said.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פָשֵׁיט רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ בְּזָב, בָּעֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea from Steps 20–21 that a minor can be a זב, and asks about one detail of that.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a minor זב's first discharge make things impure by touch, the way an adult's does?

steps.title: The two sides of ריש לקיש's question
steps.stepSummary: Side one: the first discharge works like semen, and a boy's semen is not impure, so his first discharge isn't either. Side two: it can join with a second discharge, so it matters and does make things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone whose semen makes things impure, his first discharge makes things impure. This boy's semen does not make things impure, so his first discharge shouldn't either. Or maybe, since if he sees two discharges they join together, the first one does make things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two ways to think about the question. It does not decide yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one ties the first discharge to semen because of the פסוק, and a minor's semen is not impure. Side two says the boy's first discharge clearly counts for something, because together with a second discharge it makes him a full זב. If it counts there, maybe it also makes things impure on its own, like an adult's.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or perhaps', which introduces the other side of a question
It joins together (with another discharge)
Two (discharges)

phrases.english: Anyone whose semen makes things impure,
phrases.notes: The corrected text leaves out the word in round brackets and uses the word in square brackets instead. Both mean 'makes impure'.

phrases.english: his first discharge makes things impure;

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי כֵּיוָן דְּשִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁלּוֹ לֹא מְטַמְּאָה
phrases.english: and this boy, since his semen does not make things impure,
his first discharge also should not make things impure.
Or perhaps,
since if he were to see two discharges,
the first would join with the second, it does make things impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question asked in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should the minor's first discharge be judged by his semen (not impure), or by the fact that it joins with a second discharge (impure)?

steps.title: רבא's proof: a minor is like an adult, so his first discharge makes things impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the teaching that ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״ includes adult and minor equally. Since an adult's first discharge makes things impure, so does a minor's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: come and hear. ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״ includes both adult and minor. Just as an adult's first discharge makes things impure, so too a minor's first discharge makes things impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers ריש לקיש's question using the same פסוק that included minors. The answer is that the minor's first discharge does make things impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that brings minors into the laws of זב puts them on the same level as adults. So whatever is true of an adult's first discharge is true of a minor's. The fact that a boy's semen is not impure does not change this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as ... so too', a direct comparison

steps.whatToRemember: A minor זב is treated exactly like an adult זב: his first discharge makes things impure by touch.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same פסוק used in Step 21 to include minors also gives them the full, equal laws of an adult זב.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
"This is the law of the zav"
means whether an adult or a minor.

phrases.aramaic: מָה גָּדוֹל — רְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁלּוֹ מְטַמְּאָה,
phrases.english: Just as an adult's first discharge makes things impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף קָטָן — רְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה נָמֵי מְטַמְּאָה.
phrases.english: so too a minor's first discharge also makes things impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question from Steps 22–23 in favor of the second side.
steps.raayaObject: That a minor זב's first discharge makes things impure by touch
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַזָּב״ includes both adult and minor, which makes them equal

steps.title: Does a leper's first discharge make things impure by carrying?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether the first discharge of a מצורע makes things impure through carrying, or only through touch like an ordinary person's first discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked: The first sighting of a discharge by a מצורע, does it make things impure through carrying? Is the place of the discharge counted as a 'source' that makes things impure, or is it not a source?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף raises a new question: does a מצורע's very first discharge make things impure even by carrying?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an ordinary person, the first discharge only makes things impure by touch, like semen. But a מצורע's body fluids (his מעיינות) are already known to make things impure. The question is whether the place the discharge comes from counts as one of those 'sources'. If it does, even the first discharge of a מצורע would make things impure by carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity passed on by carrying, even without touching
A 'source': a body fluid that makes things impure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'touch' and 'carrying'. Everyone agrees the first discharge makes things impure by touch. The only question is whether, for a מצורע, it also makes things impure by carrying.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef asked:
The first sighting of a discharge of a leper,
what is the law: does it make things impure through carrying?
phrases.notes: An ordinary person's first discharge makes things impure only by touch, as the earlier steps said.

phrases.english: Is the place of the discharge a 'source', so it makes things impure,
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא learned that a מצורע's body fluids, his 'sources', make things impure.

phrases.english: or perhaps it is not a 'source'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like the question about a minor's first discharge (steps 22-24), this asks about a first discharge, now for a מצורע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מצורע's first discharge counts as a 'source' (מעיין) and so makes things impure through carrying.

steps.title: רבא brings the verse 'his discharge is impure'
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts a proof from a teaching on the פסוק ״זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא הוּא״, which says that the discharge itself is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. ״זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא הוּא״, 'his discharge is impure.' This teaches about the discharge that it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to answer רב יוסף's question by quoting a teaching on a פסוק about the discharge being impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says the discharge itself is impure, meaning it makes things impure even by carrying. רבא will now ask which person this פסוק is talking about. Whose discharge it is will answer רב יוסף's question.

keyTerms.meaning: The discharge of a זב
It teaches (the פסוק teaches a law)
Impure

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear,
"his discharge is impure"
teaches about the discharge that it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a proof to answer רב יוסף's question.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's question about a מצורע's first discharge.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching on the פסוק ״זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא הוּא״ (ויקרא 15:2).

steps.title: Which case is the verse talking about?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks which case the פסוק is talking about and begins with the first option: a plain זב who is not a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what case is it speaking? If you say it is speaking about just a plain זב...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא begins testing which person the פסוק could be talking about, starting with an ordinary זב. The גמרא checks this option on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is using a process of elimination. He first suggests the פסוק is about an ordinary זב who is not also a מצורע. The next amud examines whether that reading works.

keyTerms.meaning: About what case? (asks which situation is meant)
If you say (brings up an option to test it)
Just, plain, by itself

phrases.english: About what case?
If you say it is about just a plain זב,
phrases.notes: He means a זב who is not also a מצורע. The גמרא finishes this thought on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case the פסוק quoted in step 26 is about. This sets up the elimination of options.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person the פסוק ״זוֹבוֹ טָמֵא הוּא״ is talking about, starting with the option of a plain זב.
